points.description: Top of the stack is kept at the head (beginning) of the linked list, so push and pop add/remove elements at the beginning of the list.
points.partial_credit: Award about 2-3 marks if the student says a linked list is used with push/pop at one end but does not say it is the head/beginning, or only says the top points to the head without describing push/pop.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the top of the stack is the head of the linked list and push/pop work at the beginning, in any wording, however brief. Part marks for a linked-list stack with push/pop at one end but the end is unspecified or vague. No marks for answers that do not use a linked list or only define what a stack is.
